title: Cancel a vehicle registration within NSW
summary: Registered vehicle operators can cancel their vehicle registration and hand in the number plates at a Service NSW Centre.
intro:
If you're the registered operator of a vehicle, you can cancel your registration and hand in the vehicle's number plates, at a Service NSW Centre.

There's a cancellation fee, but you're able to apply for a refund of any unused portion of the motor vehicle tax.
who_can_apply: You must be the registered operator of the vehicle.
what_you_need: The vehicle's number plates (or a Police Event Number if the plates have been lost, stolen, or destroyed)
If the vehicle was written-off or stolen, a document from the Police or insurance company with the date of the incident.

how_to_steps.text: Ensure you have all the required documents.
Visit a service centre, lodge your application, and return the vehicle's number plates.

more_info.text: If you want to keep the plates after you cancel your vehicle's registration, you'll need to put them in reserve at a service centre. Additional fees may apply.
If your vehicle is registered in joint names, you only need the signature of the primary operator.

faqs.q: What happens to my motor vehicle tax?
faqs.a: There is a cancellation fee, but you may be able to apply for a refund of any unused portion of the motor vehicle tax.

faqs.q: What do I need to cancel my registration?
faqs.a: You need the vehicle's registration certificate (if available), the number plates (or a Police Event Number if lost, stolen, or destroyed), proof of identity, fee payment, and the required PDF forms.

faqs.q: How do I cancel my vehicle registration?
faqs.a: First, download and complete the required PDF form. Then, ensure you have all necessary documents. Finally, visit a Service Centre, lodge your application, and return the vehicle's number plates.
